message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to building a well‑rounded leg routine—no function call needed!  

---

## 1️⃣ Core Compound Movements  
These recruit multiple joints and muscle groups, making them the most efficient for strength and hypertrophy.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Key Tips |
|----------|-----------------|----------|
| **Back Squat** | Quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, core | Keep your chest up, knees tracking over toes, descend to at least parallel. |
| **Front Squat** | Quads, core, upper back | Hold the bar on the front deltoids, elbows high, maintain a neutral spine. |
| **Deadlift (Conventional)** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps | Drive through heels, keep the bar close to the shins, avoid rounding the lower back. |
| **Sumo Deadlift** | Inner thighs, glutes, quads | Wider stance, toes slightly out, focus on pulling through the hips. |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | One foot elevated behind you; keep torso upright, descend until the front thigh is parallel. |
| **Hip Thrust / Glute Bridge** | Glutes, hamstrings | Squeeze at the top, avoid hyperextending the lower back. |

> **Progression**: Start with bodyweight or light dumbbells, then add a barbell or weighted vest as you master form.

---

## 2️⃣ Isolation & Functional Movements  
Great for targeting specific muscles and improving joint stability.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Key Tips |
|----------|-----------------|----------|
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Adjust foot placement to target different areas; avoid locking knees. |
| **Hamstring Curl (Machine or Stability Ball)** | Hamstrings | Control the eccentric phase; keep hips lifted for full range. |
| **Calf Raise (Standing or Seated)** | Gastrocnemius, soleus | Full stretch at the bottom, pause at the top for contraction. |
| **Step‑Up** | Quads, glutes | Use a stable platform; drive through the heel of the stepping foot. |
| **Lateral Lunge** | Inner/outer thighs, glutes | Keep the knee tracking over the toes of the stepping foot. |
| **Pistol Squat (Assisted if needed)** | Quads, glutes, core | Use a box or support for balance; focus on depth and control. |

---

## 3️⃣ Mobility & Recovery  
Essential for long‑term performance and injury prevention.

| Activity | Benefit | How to Do It |
|----------|---------|--------------|
| **Dynamic Warm‑Up** (leg swings, walking lunges) | Activates muscles, increases blood flow | 5–10 min before lifting. |
| **Foam Rolling** (quads, IT band, calves) | Releases muscle tightness | 1–2 min per muscle group. |
| **Static Stretching** (hamstrings, quads, calves) | Improves flexibility | Hold 20–30 sec after workouts. |
| **Yoga Flow** (Downward Dog, Pigeon Pose) | Enhances hip mobility | 10–15 min post‑workout or on rest days. |

---

## 4️⃣ Sample Weekly Plan (3‑Day Split)

| Day | Focus | Example Sets/Reps |
|-----|-------|-------------------|
| **Monday – Strength** | Squats, Deadlifts, Calf Raises | 4×6–8 (heavy), 3×12 (calves) |
| **Wednesday – Hypertrophy** | Front Squat, Leg Press, Hamstring Curl | 3×10–12, 3×15 (curls) |
| **Friday – Power & Functional** | Bulgarian Split Squat, Hip Thrust, Step‑Up | 3×8–10, 3×12 (step‑ups) |

> **Rest**: 48–72 hrs between sessions.  
> **Nutrition**: Aim for a protein intake of ~1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight to support recovery.  
> **Progressive Overload**: Add 2.5–5 kg to the bar or increase reps by 1–2 each week.

---

## 5️⃣ Quick Form Checklist

| Checkpoint | What to Look For |
|------------|------------------|
| **Knee Alignment** | Knees should track over toes, not collapse inward. |
| **Core Engagement** | Tighten abs throughout the movement. |
| **Breathing** | Inhale on the eccentric (lowering) phase, exhale on the concentric (lifting) phase. |
| **Tempo** | 2–3 seconds down, 1–2 seconds up for controlled strength work. |
| **Footwear** | Flat, supportive shoes for squats; cushioned for running or plyometrics. |

---

### Final Thought
Mix these exercises based on your goals—strength, size, or functional fitness—and always prioritize form over weight. If you’re new, consider a session with a qualified trainer to get personalized feedback. Happy training!
